plugin.name: Proxmox VE
plugin.description: Manage Proxmox VE from Termix: virtual machines, containers, storage, network, backups, firewall, access and the cluster.

view.title: View Proxmox
view.description: See nodes, guests, storage, charts and tasks on Proxmox hosts you can connect to.

operate.title: Operate Proxmox guests
operate.description: Start, stop, shut down, reboot, suspend and resume VMs and containers. Needs edit access to the host.

console.title: Open Proxmox consoles
console.description: Open the screen of a VM and a root shell in a container. Needs edit access to the host.

configure.title: Configure Proxmox
configure.description: Create, clone, migrate, convert and delete VMs and containers. Needs edit access to the host.

administer.title: Administer Proxmox
administer.description: Manage users, groups, roles, pools, 2FA, tokens, realms and the cluster. Needs edit access to the host.

enable.label: Proxmox node
enable.description: Mark this host as a Proxmox VE node. It then shows in the Proxmox tool under Tools.

transport.label: Connect through
transport.description: Automatic uses the API over an SSH tunnel once a token is saved, and pvesh over SSH until then.

tokenId.label: API token ID
tokenId.description: Made in Proxmox under Datacenter, Permissions, API Tokens. Looks like user@realm!name.

tokenSecret.label: API token secret
tokenSecret.description: Shown once when the token is made. Stored encrypted.

apiHost.label: API address
apiHost.description: API directly only. Leave empty to use this host's address.

caCert.label: CA certificate
caCert.description: API directly only. The node's CA in PEM, from /etc/pve/pve-root-ca.pem. Leave empty if the API has a publicly trusted certificate.

importSync.label: Keep imported guests in sync
importSync.description: Updates names, addresses and tags of the guests imported from this node, and tags the ones removed from Proxmox as proxmox-missing.

importAddNew.label: Add new guests on sync
importAddNew.description: Imports guests created in Proxmox after the first import, with the defaults last used in the import dialog.

app.pickResource: Pick a node, guest or storage on the left
app.noHostsHint: Open a host's settings, turn on Proxmox node under SSH, and pick how to connect. The node then shows here.

errors.tlsUntrusted: Termix does not trust the node's certificate. In the host's Proxmox settings, paste the node's CA from /etc/pve/pve-root-ca.pem into CA certificate, or pick API over SSH tunnel.
errors.tlsHostname: The node's certificate is for another name. Set API address to a name or address the certificate lists.
errors.tlsExpired: The node's certificate has expired or is not valid yet. Renew it in Proxmox under the node, System, Certificates.
errors.notEnabled: This host is not marked as a Proxmox node. Turn on Proxmox node in the host's settings.
errors.hostAccess: You need edit access to this host to change it.

confirm.description: This cuts the power like pulling the plug. Work that is not saved in the guest is lost.

clone.title: Clone {{name}}
clone.label: Clone {{source}} to {{id}}
clone.fullHint: Copies every disk, so the clone does not depend on the original.
clone.linkedHint: Off makes a linked clone that shares the template's disks and is made in seconds.

migrate.title: Migrate {{name}}
migrate.label: Migrate {{name}} to {{target}}
migrate.noOtherNodes: There is no other online node in this cluster to move it to.
migrate.onlineHint: The VM is running and moves live, without stopping.
migrate.restartHint: The container is running. It stops, moves and starts again on the target.

template.description: A template can't be started, only cloned. This can't be undone.
template.label: Convert {{name}} to a template

delete.title: Delete {{name}}
delete.label: Delete {{name}}
delete.warning: This deletes guest {{vmid}} and its disks. It can't be undone.
delete.stopFirst: Stop the guest before deleting it.
delete.purge: Remove from backup jobs, replication and HA
delete.purgeHint: Leaves no jobs pointing at a guest that is gone.
delete.unreferencedHint: Disks on enabled storages with this ID that the config does not list.

create.noTemplates: No container templates on this node. Download one in Proxmox under a storage, CT Templates.
create.unprivilegedHint: Safer: root in the container is not root on the node.
create.loginHint: Set a root password, SSH keys, or both.

problem.vmid: Pick an ID of 100 or more.
problem.hostname: Enter a hostname: letters, digits and dashes.
problem.name: Enter a name: letters, digits and dashes.
problem.memory: Enter at least 16 MiB of memory.
problem.swap: Enter swap in MiB, 0 for none.
problem.network: Pick a bridge and, for a static address, enter it like 192.168.0.60/24.
problem.login: Set a root password or SSH keys so you can log in.
problem.password: The password needs at least 5 characters.

hardware.pendingHint: Changes marked Pending apply when the guest restarts from Proxmox: a reboot inside the guest is not enough.
hardware.cpulimitHint: 0 for no limit. 1.5 is one and a half cores of time.
hardware.balloonHint: With the balloon driver the guest gives memory back down to this. Equal to memory turns it off, 0 removes the driver.
hardware.discardHint: Lets the guest free unused blocks on thin storage.

resize.title: Grow {{key}}
resize.noShrink: Disks can only grow. The guest's partition and file system need growing inside the guest afterwards, unless it does that on boot.
resize.label: Grow {{key}} by {{size}} GiB

move.title: Move {{key}}
move.deleteSourceHint: Off keeps it as an unused disk.
move.label: Move {{key}} to {{storage}}

detach.title: Detach {{key}}?
detach.description: The disk stays on its storage as an unused disk and can be deleted or attached again.

unused.title: Delete {{volume}}?
unused.description: This deletes the disk and everything on it. It can't be undone.

nic.heading: Network adapters
nic.name: Name in the container
nic.removeDescription: The guest loses this adapter and its address.

problem.cpu: Enter at least one socket and core.
problem.cpulimit: The CPU limit goes from 0 to 8192.
problem.memory: Enter at least 16 MiB of memory.
problem.balloon: Minimum memory can't be more than memory.
problem.swap: Enter swap in MiB, 0 for none.
problem.noSlot: Every slot of this kind is taken.
problem.size: Enter a size in whole GiB.
problem.path: Enter an absolute path like /data, not / itself.
problem.tag: A VLAN tag goes from 1 to 4094.
problem.rate: Enter a rate above 0, or leave it empty.
problem.name: Enter a name like eth0.
problem.ip4: Enter the address like 192.168.0.60/24 and a valid gateway.

hardware.detached: {{key}} detached; it stays as an unused disk
hardware.coresHint: Empty uses every core of the node.

options.protectionHint: Blocks deleting the guest and its disks until turned off.
options.agentHint: Turn on once the agent runs in the guest, for its addresses and clean shutdowns.

problem.name: Enter a name.
problem.startup: Order and delays are whole numbers.
problem.tags: Tags use letters, digits, dashes, dots and underscores.
problem.nameserver: Enter IP addresses separated by spaces.

cloudinit.noDrive: This VM has no cloud-init drive. Add one, then set the user, keys and network here; the guest image must support cloud-init.
cloudinit.usernameHint: Empty uses the image's default user.
cloudinit.passwordHint: Empty keeps the current one. Stored hashed by Proxmox.
cloudinit.regenerateHint: Writes the settings to {{drive}}. The guest reads them on its next boot.

problem.url: Enter an http or https URL.
problem.filename: The file name uses letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores.
problem.extension: ISO images end in .iso or .img; templates in .tar.gz, .tar.xz or .tar.zst.
problem.checksum: Pick a checksum type and enter the checksum in hex, or leave both empty.

delete.title: Delete {{name}}?
delete.description: This deletes the file from the storage. It can't be undone.

entries.title: Storage
entries.hint: The datacenter's storage list. Removing an entry leaves the data where it is; Proxmox just stops using it.
entries.removeDescription: Proxmox stops using it. The files, volumes and backups on it stay; guests whose disks are there stop working until it is added back.

pbs.idFormat: a letter, then letters, digits, ., - or _
pbs.namespaceHint: Optional: a namespace inside the datastore.
pbs.passwordHint: Left empty when editing, the saved one stays.
pbs.fingerprintHint: From the PBS dashboard's Show Fingerprint. Needed when its certificate is self-signed.

confirm.description: Proxmox's own services keep the node and its API running; stopping one can cut off this tool until it starts again.

updates.installHint: Install upgrades from the node's terminal with apt full-upgrade; Proxmox does not upgrade through its API.

none.directory: No directory storage on a disk of its own.

storage.wipeWarning: The chosen disks are partitioned and formatted. Only disks with nothing on them are offered.
storage.name: Name
storage.noUnused: There is no unused disk. Wipe one under Disks first, if what is on it can go.
storage.addStorageHint: Makes it a Proxmox storage of the same name, for disks, containers or backups.

problem.name: A name starts with a letter and has letters, digits, -, _ or .
problem.tooFew: This RAID level needs at least {{count}} disks.
problem.even: RAID10 needs an even number of disks.

storage.removeWarning: Guests with disks on it lose them. Removing does not move anything off it first.
storage.cleanupDisksHint: Erases the disks so they can be used again.

inUse.lvm: It still has logical volumes. Remove them first; this group may hold the node's own system.
inUse.lvmthin: It still holds data. Move or remove the guest disks on it first.

disks.gptDescription: Writes an empty GPT partition table to the disk.
disks.wipeWarning: Erases the partition table and every filesystem, LVM and ZFS signature on the disk (now: {{used}}). What is on it is gone for good.
disks.wipeInUse: In use. Remove the volume group, pool, directory or storage on it first.

power.termixWarning: If Termix runs on this node, it goes down too until the node is back.

reboot.title: Reboot {{node}}?
reboot.label: Reboot {{node}}
reboot.warning_one: {{count}} running guest stops or shuts down first, as its startup settings say.
reboot.warning_other: {{count}} running guests stop or shut down first, as their startup settings say.

shutdown.title: Shut down {{node}}?
shutdown.label: Shut down {{node}}
shutdown.warning_one: {{count}} running guest goes down with it, and nothing starts it again until someone powers the node on.
shutdown.warning_other: {{count}} running guests go down with it, and nothing starts them again until someone powers the node on.

nodes.shellHint: Opens this host's SSH terminal in Termix.

problem.search: Enter a search domain, such as example.com.
problem.server: A DNS server is an IPv4 or IPv6 address.
problem.noServer: Enter at least one DNS server.

time.title: Time
time.hint: The clock itself is kept by NTP (chrony) on the node.

hosts.title: Hosts
hosts.warning: The node's own name must keep resolving to its address, or the cluster and its web interface stop working.

certs.title: Certificates
certs.chainHint: PEM: the node's certificate first, then the intermediates.
certs.keyHint: PEM, unencrypted. Leave empty to keep the key already on the node.
certs.badCert: This is not a PEM certificate.
certs.badKey: This is not a PEM private key.
certs.restart: Restart the web interface to use it
certs.restartHint: pveproxy restarts; Termix loses the API for a few seconds.
certs.removeDescription: The node goes back to its self-signed certificate, and the web interface restarts.

repos.hint: Run Refresh package lists under Packages after a change. The Enterprise repositories need a subscription.

acme.title: ACME
acme.noDomains: No domains yet. Edit to add the names this node answers to.
acme.httpHint: The HTTP challenge needs port 80 of this node reachable from the internet under the domain. DNS works without that, and for wildcards.
acme.hint: Accounts and plugins are shared by the whole cluster; domains are per node.

problem.tooMany: A node has up to six ACME domains.
problem.domain: A domain is a full name such as pve.example.com.
problem.wildcard: A wildcard domain needs a DNS challenge plugin.

account.title: Account
account.name: Name
account.eabHint: Only for CAs that ask for External Account Binding.
account.removeDescription: The account is deactivated at the CA and removed here. Certificates already issued keep working.

problem.name: A name has letters, digits, -, _ or .
problem.directory: The directory is an http or https URL.
problem.tos: Accept the terms of service to register.
problem.eab: EAB needs both the key ID and the HMAC key.

plugin.delayHint: How long to wait for the TXT record to spread.
plugin.noFields: Proxmox lists no fields for this provider; see acme.sh's docs for the variables it reads.
plugin.none: No DNS plugins. HTTP works without one.
plugin.removeDescription: Domains that use it can no longer be validated.

notes.title: Notes
notes.empty: No notes. Proxmox shows them on the node's summary.

options.title: Options
options.delayHint: Seconds to wait after the node boots before starting guests set to start on boot. Empty for none.
options.wakeonlanHint: The node's network card, so another cluster node can wake it.

problem.mac: Enter a MAC address like aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff.

console.openHint: Opens the guest's Termix host, or offers to add it to Termix first.
console.pick: Open a console from a running VM or container in the Proxmox tool.
console.notRunning: Start the guest to open its console.
console.proxmoxHint: Proxmox's own console through the node: the screen of a VM, a shell in a container. For a guest with no network yet.

sdn.hint: SDN zones, VNets and subnets come with cluster management in a later release.

network.hint: Changes are saved to /etc/network/interfaces.new and take effect on Apply, which reloads the node's network.
network.name: Name
network.vlanAwareHint: Lets guests on this bridge use VLAN tags.

nameHint.bridge: vmbr followed by a number, like vmbr1.
nameHint.bond: bond followed by a number, like bond0.
nameHint.vlan: device.tag like vmbr0.10, or vlan10 with a raw device.

network.addressWarning: This interface carries the address Termix reaches the node on. A mistake can cut Termix off until someone fixes the node at its console.
network.removeDescription: The interface is removed when the change is applied.
network.applyDescription: The node reloads its network. If the new settings are wrong, the node and Termix's connection to it can go offline.

problem.gateway: A gateway needs an IPv4 address and a valid gateway IP.
problem.ports: Enter interface names separated by spaces.
problem.slaves: A bond needs at least one slave.
problem.vlanDevice: Name the raw device for a vlanN interface.

name.bridge: A bridge is named vmbr and a number.
name.bond: A bond is named bond and a number.
name.vlan: A VLAN is named device.tag or vlan and a number.

import.title: Import guests as Termix hosts
import.hint: Each chosen VM or container becomes a Termix host, tagged proxmox. Importing also refreshes the names, addresses and tags of guests imported before, and tags the ones gone from Proxmox as proxmox-missing.
import.loading: Looking for guests and their addresses…
import.none: This cluster has no VMs or containers.
import.folderSearch: Search or create, / for a subfolder
import.desktopHint: Needs the Remote Desktop plugin to connect.
import.syncHint: Turn on Keep imported guests in sync in the host's Proxmox settings to refresh them on a schedule.
import.addHint: This guest is not a Termix host yet. Add it to open its terminal, then Console opens it straight away.
import.gone: Proxmox no longer lists this guest.

snapshots.hint: A snapshot keeps the guest's disks and settings as they are now, on storage that supports snapshots.
snapshots.name: Name
snapshots.nameHint: A letter, then letters, digits, - or _, up to 40 characters.
snapshots.vmstateHint: Rolling back then resumes the VM where it was. Takes longer and needs space for the memory.

problem.format: Start with a letter; use letters, digits, - and _, 2 to 40 characters.
problem.taken: A snapshot with this name exists.

snapshots.rollbackDescription: {{vmid}} goes back to how it was at {{name}}. Everything that changed since is lost. A running guest is stopped first.
snapshots.deleteDescription: The guest keeps running as it is; only the saved state {{name}} goes.

summary.title: Cluster
summary.noQuorum: No: changes are blocked until enough nodes are back
summary.joinHint: Paste this into Proxmox's Join Cluster dialog on the new node. It holds this node's address and certificate fingerprint, not a password.
summary.createHint: This node is not in a cluster. Create one in Proxmox's web interface or with pvecm create on the node; joining needs the other node's root password, so Termix leaves it to Proxmox.
summary.noJoin: Proxmox gave no node to join through.
summary.copyFailed: The browser did not allow copying; select the text and copy it.

backup.jobsHint: Scheduled backups for the whole cluster. Each runs on the nodes where its guests are.
backup.deleteJobDescription: Backups it already made stay on their storage.
backup.runDescription: Starts the backups on {{nodes}}. Guests in snapshot mode keep running.
backup.notBackedUpHint: VMs and containers no job includes.
backup.allBackedUp: Every guest is in a backup job.

job.scheduleHint: A Proxmox calendar event: 21:00, sat 02:00, mon..fri 23:30 or */6:00.
job.nodeHint: Empty: every node backs up its own guests.
job.notesHint: A template for each backup's notes. guestname, node, vmid and cluster written in double curly braces are filled in.

backup.modeHint: Snapshot keeps the guest running; Stop gives the most consistent backup.
backup.noStorage: No storage on this node holds backups. Add one, such as a Proxmox Backup Server, under Datacenter, Storage.
backup.none: No backups of this guest yet.
backup.protectedHint: Pruning and deleting leave it alone until protection is taken off.
backup.restoreStorageHint: Empty: the storage each disk was on.
backup.uniqueHint: So the copy and the original can run side by side.
backup.overwriteWarning: Everything on {{vmid}} now, disks included, is replaced by the backup.
backup.stopFirst: Stop {{vmid}} first: Proxmox only restores over a stopped guest.
backup.overwriteDescription: The guest's current disks and settings are deleted and the backup takes their place. This can't be undone.
backup.deleteDescription: It is removed from {{storage}} for good.

replication.title: Replication jobs
replication.hint: Copies a guest's ZFS disks to another node on a schedule, so it can start there quickly.
replication.singleNode: Replication copies disks to another node. This cluster has one node, so there is nowhere to copy to yet.
replication.scheduleHint: A Proxmox calendar event; */15 is every 15 minutes.
replication.deleteDescription: Proxmox also removes the copied disks from {{target}}.

ha.resourcesSectionHint: Guests HA keeps running: if their node fails, another node starts them.
ha.noResources: No guests are managed by HA.
ha.stateHint: What HA keeps the guest in. Ignored hands it back to you.
ha.removeDescription: The guest keeps its current state; it just won't be restarted elsewhere if its node fails.
ha.rulesHint: Where HA may run guests: on preferred nodes, together, or apart.
ha.ruleIdFormat: a letter, then letters, digits, - or _
ha.resourcesHint: HA names, like vm:100 or ct:101, separated by commas.
ha.resourcesFormat: vm:ID or ct:ID, separated by commas
ha.nodesHint: node or node:priority, separated by commas; higher priority wins.
ha.nodesFormat: node names, each with an optional :priority
ha.strictHint: Only these nodes; without it, others are used when none of them is up.

warning.cluster: The datacenter switch turns the firewall on for every node. Proxmox keeps port 8006 and SSH open from the local network, but check the rules before turning it on.
warning.node: The node's firewall only runs while the datacenter firewall is on.
warning.guest: Also needs Firewall ticked on the guest's network adapter, and the datacenter firewall on.

firewall.enableDescription: Every node starts filtering with these rules. If they block the address Termix uses, Termix loses the node until someone fixes it at its console.
firewall.rulesHint: Checked from the top; the first matching rule decides.

rule.macroHint: A Proxmox macro such as SSH, HTTPS or Ping sets the protocol and ports.
rule.addressHint: An address, network, alias or +ipset; empty for any.

firewall.groupsHint: Rule sets nodes and guests can use as one rule.
firewall.deleteGroupDescription: Proxmox refuses while a rule still uses it.
firewall.aliasesHint: Names for addresses and networks, to use in rules.
firewall.deleteAliasDescription: Proxmox refuses while a rule still uses it.
firewall.ipsetsHint: Lists of addresses rules can name as +set.

ipset.name: Name
ipset.nomatchHint: Leaves this address out of the set.

firewall.deleteIpsetDescription: Remove its entries first; Proxmox refuses while a rule still uses it.
firewall.nameFormat: a letter, then letters, digits, - or _

access.needsAdminister: Changes here need the Administer Proxmox permission and are written to the audit log.
access.nameFormat: a letter, then letters, digits, ., - or _
access.secretOnce: Proxmox shows this once. Store it now; it can't be read again.

user.hint: Users of Proxmox's web interface and API. pam users are the node's Linux users.
user.passwordHint: For the pve realm. pam users use their Linux password.
user.pamWarning: This changes the Linux password of the user on the node, root included.
user.deleteDescription: Their tokens and permissions go too.

token.hint: API tokens for scripts and tools such as Termix. With privilege separation, a token only has the permissions given to it.
token.privsepHint: Off gives the token all of its user's rights.
token.deleteDescription: Anything using it, Termix included, stops getting in.

tfa.hint: Second factors for signing in to Proxmox. Tokens don't use them.
tfa.secretHint: Enter the secret, or the otpauth link, in an authenticator app.
tfa.codeHint: The six digits the app shows now.
tfa.passwordHint: Proxmox asks for it when you change your own second factors.
tfa.deleteDescription: With no other factor left, signing in needs only the password.
tfa.recoveryHint: One-time keys for when the authenticator is lost. Making new ones replaces the user's old keys, and they are shown only once.

group.hint: Groups make it easier to give several users the same permissions.
group.deleteDescription: Its users stay; permissions given to the group go.

pool.hint: Pools gather guests and storage, so permissions can be given for all of them at once.
pool.deleteDescription: Proxmox refuses while it still has members.

role.hint: Sets of privileges. Built-in roles can't be changed.
role.deleteDescription: Permissions that give this role go with it.

realm.hint: Where users sign in: Linux (pam), Proxmox (pve), LDAP, Active Directory or OpenID Connect.
realm.bindPasswordHint: Left empty when editing, the saved one stays.
realm.deleteDescription: Its users can no longer sign in.

acl.hint: Who has which role where. A path like /vms/100 or /storage/local; / is everything.
acl.pathHint: / for everything, /vms/100 for one guest, /pool/web for a pool.

ceph.title: Ceph
ceph.notInstalled: Ceph is not installed on this node. Set it up with Proxmox's Ceph wizard or pveceph install on the node; Termix then shows its health here.
